headword: {窮地|きゅうち}に{陥|おちい}る
gloss: to fall into a predicament; to find oneself in a tight spot

definitions.gloss: to fall into a predicament; to find oneself in a desperate situation
definitions.explanation: To end up in a very difficult or desperate situation from which it is hard to escape.

examples.japanese: {窮地|きゅうち}に{陥|おちい}った。
examples.english: I found myself in a tight spot.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{経営|けいえい}の{窮地|きゅうち}に{陥|おちい}った。
examples.english: The company fell into a management crisis.

examples.japanese: {判断|はんだん}を{誤|あやま}ったことで、チーム{全体|ぜんたい}が{窮地|きゅうち}に{陥|おちい}ってしまった。
examples.english: A misjudgment caused the entire team to fall into a desperate situation.

notes:
{窮地|きゅうち} means a dire situation or predicament, and {陥|おちい}る means to fall into. A set expression common in news and formal writing.

RELATED WORDS:
- {窮地|きゅうち}に{立|た}たされる: to be driven into a corner (passive — someone else puts you there)
- {窮地|きゅうち}を{脱|だっ}する: to escape a predicament
- {窮地|きゅうち}に{追|お}い{込|こ}む: to drive someone into a corner
- {危機|きき}に{陥|おちい}る: to fall into crisis (similar pattern)

USAGE:
Implies a serious, difficult-to-escape situation. Stronger than {困|こま}る (to be troubled) and more formal than ピンチ (a pinch).
